T1040.description: Adversaries may sniff network traffic to capture information, including authentication credentials or sensitive data passed in cleartext over unencrypted WiFi networks.
T1040.detection: Monitor for promisc/monitor mode interfaces, open WiFi network usage without VPN/TLS encryption, and cleartext protocols.
T1040.mitigation: Enforce WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2 with 802.1X; mandate full-tunnel VPN with mutual authentication on all untrusted networks.

T1557.description: Adversaries may attempt to position themselves between two or more networked devices to support follow-on behaviors such as network eavesdropping or data manipulation.
T1557.detection: Detect rogue APs with matching SSIDs, duplicate default gateways, anomalous ARP replies, and rogue DHCP servers.
T1557.mitigation: Deploy 802.1X network access control with certificate-based EAP-TLS; use static ARP or Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI); enable DHCP snooping.

T1557.002.description: Adversaries may poison Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) caches by sending spoofed ARP gratuitous replies to reroute traffic through an attacker host.
T1557.002.detection: Monitor for rapid MAC flapping for the default gateway IP, duplicate IP notifications, and unsolicited gratuitous ARP replies.
T1557.002.mitigation: Configure static ARP tables for critical gateways; enable Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) on managed switches; inspect gateway MAC drift.

T1565.002.description: Adversaries may alter data in transit, such as forging DNS responses or injecting content into unencrypted HTTP/TCP sessions.
T1565.002.detection: Compare system resolver answers against DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) trusted canary resolvers; inspect DNS response TTL and duplicate replies.
T1565.002.mitigation: Enforce DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) or DNS-over-TLS (DoT) with DNSSEC validation; block unencrypted UDP port 53 outbound at boundary.

T1498.001.technique_name: Network Denial of Service: Direct Network Flood
T1498.001.description: Adversaries may flood wireless networks with 802.11 Deauthentication or Disassociation frames to force client disconnection and capture 4-way WPA handshakes.
T1498.001.detection: Detect high-rate 802.11 deauth/disassociation frames (>10 frames/sec) or broadcast deauth frames (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF).
T1498.001.mitigation: Deploy 802.11w Protected Management Frames (PMF) on APs and endpoints; mandate WPA3 which requires PMF.

T1110.002.description: Adversaries may capture EAPOL 4-way handshakes or PMKID elements from wireless beacon/association frames for offline dictionary or brute-force cracking.
T1110.002.detection: Correlate sudden deauthentication bursts immediately followed by EAPOL handshake frame captures.
T1110.002.mitigation: Use complex, high-entropy pre-shared keys (>20 characters) or migrate to 802.1X EAP-TLS with client certificates; disable PMKID caching on legacy APs.

T1552.001.technique_name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files / Cleartext
T1552.001.description: Adversaries may harvest authentication credentials transmitted over plaintext protocols (HTTP Basic Auth, FTP, Telnet, POP3, IMAP) over untrusted networks.
T1552.001.detection: Deep packet inspection for Authorization headers, FTP USER/PASS strings, and unencrypted login signatures.
T1552.001.mitigation: Enforce HTTPS/TLS for all corporate services; use HSTS preloading; prohibit cleartext legacy protocols.

T1562.001.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
T1562.001.description: Adversaries may strip SSL/TLS encryption (SSL stripping, SSLstrip+) or present untrusted self-signed root certificates to intercept secure communications.
T1562.001.detection: Detect HTTP 302 redirects from HTTPS to HTTP, stripped Strict-Transport-Security headers, or untrusted/drifted TLS certificate fingerprints.
T1562.001.mitigation: Enforce HSTS with includeSubDomains and preload lists; pin TLS certificates on native clients; alert on certificate issuer drift.
